    """Merge two sorted integer lists into one sorted list in linear time."""

    while i < len(a) and j < len(b):

        else:

    return merged

A seed is like a tiny sleeping plant with a built-in food supply. When it gets the right conditions—warmth, water, and sometimes light—it wakes up. The seed’s shell softens, and the baby plant inside starts to grow.

First, the plant sends a root down into the soil to drink water and get nutrients. Then a tiny shoot pushes up toward the sunlight. The shoot grows into a stem, and leaves begin to open so the plant can use sunlight to make its own food.

As the plant keeps growing, it gets taller and stronger. Its roots spread out, its leaves catch sunlight, and it may eventually make flowers and seeds of its own. That’s how a tiny seed can become a big plant!

A seed is like a tiny sleeping baby plant wrapped in a hard shell. It has everything it needs inside to start growing, but it needs the right conditions to wake up. When a seed gets water, warmth, and sometimes light, it begins to soften and swell. This tells the plant inside that it’s time to grow.

First, the seed sends a root down into the soil to drink water and get nutrients. Then a tiny shoot pushes up toward the sunlight. The shoot grows into a stem, and leaves begin to open. Leaves are like solar panels—they catch sunlight and help the plant make its own food.

As the plant gets bigger, it keeps growing taller and stronger. It may grow flowers, and those flowers can make new seeds. When the seeds fall to the ground, the whole process can start again. That’s how a tiny seed can become a big, beautiful plant!
